item.title: Pistons lose two key players ahead of road game vs. Spurs
item.description: SAN ANTONIO — The Detroit Pistons will be significantly short-handed against the 12-2 San Antonio Spurs on Tuesday, Nov. 17, at Frost Bank Center. The Pistons announced in Monday's injury report that Ron Holland II and Duncan Robinson are out. Holland will miss the game with a left knee contusion and a bone bruise he sustained late in the fourth quarter of Saturday's 137-117 loss to the Miami Heat . Holland's injury came after Robinson was ruled out after halftime with a left quadriceps strain. Holland has had a slow start to his third season, averaging 4.9 points on 34.4% shooting. However, the former lottery pick (No. 5 overall in 2024) has found different ways to showcase his importance. In a game against the Heat, Holland had one of his most impactful performances, contributing beyond scoring. He grabbed five offensive rebounds, finished with seven boards, three assists and one steal against the Heat. Against the Spurs, Robinson's absence will leave a bigger hole for the Pistons, since he has taken the helm as the team's second-best offensive player, averaging a career-best 17.4 points on a team-best 43.1% shooting from deep, along with 1.3 steals through the first 12 games. At the time of his injury against the Heat, Robinson had established himself as one of Detroit's most productive players inside Kaseya Center, scoring 10 points and connecting on three 3-pointers. In addition to Holland and Robinson, Taurean Prince has also been ruled out with right knee soreness. All-NBA center Jalen Duren will remain sidelined with a right hamstring strain he suffered against the Heat on Oct. 23. However, the Pistons' most recent injury report offered a ray of hope, as Isaiah Joe has been upgraded to doubtful after missing nine games with a right hip contusion sustained against the Philadelphia 76ers on Oct. 25. coty.davis@detroitnews.com @cotydavis_24 This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Pistons lose two key players ahead of road game vs. Spurs

item.title: Karl-Anthony Towns ties Walt Bellamy in Knicks franchise history
item.description: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Karl-Anthony Towns ties Walt Bellamy in Knicks franchise history appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Amid a disappointing start to the season, the New York Knicks climbed back over .500 at 7-6, following their recent 112-108 win against the Toronto Raptors. During the Knicks’ win, All-Star forward Karl-Anthony Towns tied a franchise record by matching Walt Bellamy for the most double-doubles to start a season. Karl-Anthony Towns finished with 28 points, 17 rebounds and three assists in the team’s win against the Raptors, tying Bellamy for 13 double-doubles to start a season for the Knicks. Towns has continued to be a bright spot for the Knicks despite having his contract extension talks tabled by the organization for the time being. The six-time All-Star is in his third full season with the Knicks after being acquired via trade with the Minnesota Timberwolves prior to the start of the 2024-25 season. He was instrumental in the Knicks’ title run last year, securing the franchise’s first championship in over 50 years. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) This season, Towns has appeared in 13 games for the Knicks at a little over 32 minutes per game. He’s been averaging 21.6 points, a league-leading 13.9 rebounds and 3.6 assists with splits of 53.4 percent shooting from the field, 39.7 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 76.5 percent shooting from the free-throw line. Towns is also leading the league in defensive rebounds at 10.8. Should Towns and the Knicks fail to reach an agreement on a contract extension , the 12-year veteran has a player option for the 2027-28 season. If it reaches that point and he declines the option, Towns would become an unrestricted free agent. The No. 1 overall pick in the 2015 NBA Draft, Towns played the first nine seasons of his career with the Wolves. item.title: Hornets Fourth Quarter Collapse Hits New Low With Worst Rating
item.description: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images The Charlotte Hornets are bleeding points when it matters most. On Sunday, the team turned a one-point deficit into a 17-point hole before settling for an eight-point loss. This pattern is not new. The squad let a 30-point lead dwindle to just eight against the Cleveland Cavaliers earlier. They also surrendered a 23-point cushion against the Miami Heat. Offense Stalls When Games Tighten The core issue is a lack of a closer. LaMelo Ball used to be the answer, but he is gone. The current roster has no one to take over in the final minutes. Sports Illustrated notes the team simply does not have a replacement for that role. The Hornets hold the NBA’s worst offensive rating at 102.5 for the whole game. But the real disaster happens in the fourth quarter. That rating crashes to 90.1 during winning time. This figure is the worst in the league by a disturbing margin. The Milwaukee Bucks sit second at 102.0. The gap is massive. The offense is bad all game, but it falls apart completely when the clock winds down. Defense Fails at the Same Time It is not just the scoring that breaks down. The defense also gives up when the game gets close. In the fourth quarter, the Hornets hold the fourth-worst defensive rating. Their overall defensive rating is only the 16th best. The protection vanishes when it is needed most. Charles Lee, the head coach, has called out the turnovers that fuel these runs. Every starter recorded at least four turnovers in a recent loss to the Phoenix Suns. Lee told reporters, “That’s way too many opportunities for the other team to capitalize on.” Those mistakes give the opponent free shots and easy points. The team cannot stop the bleed because they cannot keep the ball. Key Players Are Not Ready Hope for a fix relies on players who are not available. Brandon Miller is still finding his rhythm and cannot buy a basket right now. Coby White is on a minutes restriction as he recovers from an injury. Kon Knueppel is sidelined. Even if these three play their best, the stats show the team is still a long way from being a playoff threat. Bad teams struggle when the lights are brightest and currently the Hornets are a bad team. The lack of a closer and the worst fourth-quarter offense in the league suggest it could be a long season for fans unless the team turns things around. The Clippers will host the reeling Hornets on Sunday in Inglewood, Calif.

item.title: Kevin Durant’s Podcast Co-Host Urges Fans to Stop Dragging Caitlin Clark Into JuJu Watkins Comparisons
item.description: Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark speaks with media members Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026, at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. © Imagn Images Almost every conversation in the WNBA world somehow always becomes about Caitlin Clark, and Kevin Durant’s podcast co-host wants it to stop. After the Toronto Tempo recently landed the first overall pick of the 2027 WNBA draft, JuJu Watkins has again found the spotlight. However, comparisons to Clark are already out on social media, and Durant’s “Boardroom” co-host Eddie Gonzalez didn’t seem impressed. Watkins and the USC Trojans faced a tough rivalry battle against the South Carolina Gamecocks, but lost the game 89-85. The senior guard scored 25 points, along with two rebounds and two blocks, but a clutch block by Jordan Lee ended the night for the Trojans. Gonzalez reshared an X post comparing Watkins and Clark, with the original poster arguing that Clark’s generational talent should not be the standard against which Watkins is measured. Gonzalez responded: “I love cc and jazzy and juju and I promise to GOD we can mention all the other basketball players without bringing up Caitlin lol Like I swear we can just talk about other players and it’s fine.” Clark has impacted the game and the league since her No. 1 selection in 2024. Besides her ability to make pinpoint passes, open the floor in transition, and score from all distances, the 2024 Rookie of the Year has also helped bring more viewership to the WNBA. Watkins is also expected to have an immediate impact on any squad. NBA star backs Caitlin Clark’s new shoes Boston Celtics guard Derrick White talked highly of Caitlin Clark’s first Nike signature shoe, Caitlin 1s, launched last month. Many sporting legends and basketball stars have shared shout-outs for Clark’s shoes and even wore them during games. Speaking on his “White Noise” podcast on YouTube, White said: “I’ve been loyal to the Sabrina for two years. I was able to get to know her at the Olympics. But Caitlin’s in my agency and I was like, ‘Yeah, I’ll rock the Caitlins when they come out,’ and I like them too. I’ve played well in them, so it’s kind of hard for me to go back. But I think I’ll be mixing between Sabrinas and Caitlin through the whole year.” Clark has garnered significant limelight, and Watkins still has a lot to do before she can be compared to the Indiana Fever guard. Only time will tell which way the USC guard’s future in the league moves in the coming months. item.title: Littler hits triple-bull, but Price checkout doesn't add up
item.description: Luke Littler (2024 and 2025) and Gerwyn Price (2018, 2019 and 2021) have both won the Grand Slam of Darts on multiple occasions [Getty Images] Gerwyn Price and Luke Littler both made it through to the Grand Slam of Darts knockout stage on a night featuring a bizarre maths error and a sensational triple-bull checkout. Littler suffered a 5-4 defeat by Dutchman Niels Zonneveld but claimed the three legs he required to progress from the group stage. The 19-year-old, egged on by the crowd at the Aldersley venue in Wolverhampton, improbably landed three darts on the bullseye to produce a remarkable 150 checkout and level the match at 4-4, only to lose the deciding leg. Price, meanwhile, claimed a 5-2 victory over Sebastian Bialecki - although he was the beneficiary of an unusual mathematical mistake. The Welshman was 2-1 up against Poland's Bialecki and required 135 to win the fourth leg. Price's first dart hit treble 19, leaving him with 78, but he asked referee Charlie Corstorphine what he had left to score and was incorrectly told 88. In good faith, Price promptly threw treble 16 and then double 20 to win the leg, having scored 145 - which should have bust him. "A rare scoring error was made by the referee in the fourth leg of the match between Gerwyn Price and Sebastian Bialecki," organisers the PDC told BBC Sport in a statement. "Under Darts Regulation Authority (DRA) rule 6.4, as the error was not corrected before the next leg began, the leg score stands as announced." Price said he was unaware of the miscalculation until it was flagged up to him before he walked into a post-match news conference. "I hit the first treble and I asked 'what have I got left?' and he said 88, so I threw treble 16 and double top, then he said 'game shot'," said fourth seed Price. "I'm glad I didn't know, because it probably would have played on my mind." What do DRA rules say about Price error? The DRA's rulebook is clear if there has been an error in scoring which, although rare in professional darts, can sometimes occur. The following clauses are what the rulebook says about the mistake involving Price: 6.4.6 Errors in arithmetic shall stand as detailed on the scoreboard unless corrected prior to the next throw of the player whose score is in error. Any error in the score can be corrected by the referee at any time until game shot is called in that leg. 6.4.7 If the incorrect score resulted in a leg win the result will stand unless corrected prior to the start of the next leg. 6.4.8 If the incorrect score resulted in the winning of a match the result will be considered as final when both players and the referee have left the playing area believing the match to be successfully completed. item.description: The Indiana Hoosiers are 9-1 and No. 9 in the College Football Playoff rankings, and the one game they lost keeps following them. Curt Cignetti used his weekly press conference on Monday to push back on how that 19-15 loss to the Ohio State Buckeyes on Oct. 17 gets framed now that Ohio State has three losses. “We knocked the quarterback out. We ripped the heart out of that team. They haven’t been the same since without the quarterback. … We missed a layup. And you know what, they won, we didn’t. The team Indiana played was the preseason No. 1, with a quarterback who finished fourth in the Heisman Trophy voting last season. The team that has gone 1-2 since is starting a freshman. A four-point loss to the first group says something different about Indiana than a loss to the second would, yet the three-loss record attached to Ohio State now looks the same to the selection committee. The Hoosiers have won three straight, including Saturday’s 27-13 win over the same USC team that beat Fahey and the Buckeyes by 12. item.title: UTEP AD Jim Senter explains Scotty Walden firing after Miners’ 6-28 run under him
item.description: The UTEP Miners fired Scotty Walden on Monday, with two games left in his third season and the program’s first in the Mountain West Conference. On3’s Pete Nakos reported the move, and athletic director Jim Senter announced that Walden had been relieved of his duties effective immediately. The Miners are 1-9 overall and 0-6 in league play, with no wins against an FBS opponent. Walden’s teams won three games in 2024, two in 2025 and one so far this fall, which leaves him 6-28 in El Paso. Defensive coordinator Kyle Beyer will serve as interim head coach for the final two games against the Air Force Falcons and the Northern Illinois Huskies. UTEP head football coach Scotty Walden hypes up his team during warm up before a game against Texas at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, Texas, on Saturday, Sept. 13, 2025. “We are grateful to Scotty for the countless hours he’s put in leading our program. His tenure has been marked by unprecedented success in recruiting and record-breaking team academic performance. He has excelled at community relations and fundraising, and has put his own money back into the program. We haven’t seen the necessary improvement from year one to year three and believe it’s time for new leadership,” Senter said . UTEP hired Walden in December 2023 on the strength of a 26-14 record at FCS Austin Peay, where his win total rose in each of his four seasons. He was 34, with an offense-first reputation, and he replaced Dana Dimel, who had been fired after five losing seasons in six years. “He will put a product on the field that Miner fans will love to watch,” Senter said when the school introduced him. The climb Walden built at Austin Peay ran in reverse in El Paso, and a coach can survive a slow build far more easily than a slide that gets worse every fall. Three wins became two, then one, in the same stretch that Senter credits with unprecedented recruiting success. What does UTEP’s next coach walk into? UTEP’s move to the Mountain West reunited the Miners with old Western Athletic Conference rivals and placed them in a league where their resources sit near the bottom, a point Walden made himself before the season started. “With us probably being the lowest revenue sharing team in the Mountain West outside of Air Force, one of the things I’m always asking the coaches is, ‘what is our edge?’ We’re going to have to be different,” Walden told Mike Craven of Dave Campbell’s Texas Football in August. UTEP head coach Scotty Walden hugs his players during the senior day celebration before the annual I-10 rivalry football game against NMSU at the Sun Bowl in El Paso, Texas, on Saturday, Nov. 22, 2025. UTEP’s 28th head coach will inherit that same budget position and a program that has not posted a winning season since 2021. The school said its national search begins immediately, and Beyer’s two games in charge include the one conference opponent Walden placed below the Miners in revenue sharing. item.description: Michigan State could be without forward Jordan Scott when it visits Tennessee on Tuesday , and Tom Izzo spent part of his Monday media session laying out who would cover for him. Izzo gave Scott a 60-70% chance of playing against the Volunteers after the sophomore picked up a shoulder injury in the Spartans’ 106-72 victory over Northern Iowa . Scott hurt his right shoulder in the first half Friday and did not play after halftime , finishing with 11 points, four rebounds and two assists in 11 minutes. Izzo said Monday that there is no structural damage in the shoulder, though Scott has been kept out of contact work. “Whether he’ll (Scott) play or not today, he didn’t do anything yesterday, just shot a little bit. He might practice a little bit today, and it just depends on how fast it comes along, to be very honest with you,” Izzo said. “He’s got almost decent range of motion now. It’s whether he gets it bumped again, what’ll happen and what doesn’t happen. So, that’s the deal on Jordan Scott.” Kaleb Glenn Could Get Jordan Scott’s Minutes Izzo said forward Kaleb Glenn could get some more run time if Scott is out, despite his offensive struggles. Glenn is still working on learning Izzo’s system after sitting out last season with a torn patellar tendon . He’s averaged 7.3 points per game on 13.3 minutes this season, but hasn’t found his rhythm from beyond the arc. He’s gone one-for-six from three this season, but Izzo still thinks he’s one of the team’s top shooters. Izzo also pointed to forward Coen Carr and guard Carlos Medlock Jr., whose roles could be adjusted if Scott sits. “To be honest with you, he (Glenn) is one of my better three-point shooters. Growing up in Oklahoma, OU is a program I’ve always known about and respected, so having the opportunity to play for the Sooners and represent my home state would be special. I think the offer shows that the coaches believe in my ability and see me fitting into what they’re building over there.” Sweat ranks as the No. 397 overall prospect in the Class of 2028, according to the Rivals Industry Ranking. item.title: JJ Gabriel: how much Real Madrid are paying to sign Man United wonderkid in January revealed
item.description: JJ Gabriel: how much Real Madrid are paying to sign Man United wonderkid in January revealed Manchester United were left in shock when their academy’s finest jewel, JJ Gabriel asked to be deregistered as he sought to leave the club. The 16-year-old cited a lack of senior minutes as the main reason, and despite INEOS’ best attempts , it looks like the England Under-17 international will join a new club in January. Multiple teams, including fierce rivals Barcelona and Real Madrid, were reportedly eyeing the Enfield-born starlet, and Los Blancos have reportedly won the race . United are reportedly due a mere €300,000 in compensation, a stance the Red Devils are likely to challenge. Total cost to sign JJ Gabriel revealed According to SPORT , the deal to sign JJ Gabriel will cost €15 million in total, and it includes a five-year contract and commissions for the intermediaries involved in the deal. His salary demands were considered significant, which saw Bayern Munich eventually leave the race . SPORT ‘s report indicates that Real Madrid accepted his terms and conditions. Source: Transfermarkt “Real Madrid’s agent, Ali Barat, is at Valdebebas to finalise the signing of JJ Gabriel. The deal, which has been well underway for several days, is entering its final phase after both parties reached a verbal agreement for the 16-year-old English talent. “The financial package includes training compensation payable to Manchester United, amounting to just over €300,000, the player’s contract for the next five seasons, and the corresponding commissions for intermediaries. In total, the outlay will exceed €15 million. United will battle the verdict “The operation, however, is not without its difficulties. Manchester United, the club to which JJ Gabriel is officially registered, is determined to challenge the move, believing it infringes on their rights to the player. “The English club is unwilling to facilitate his departure and is maintaining a firm stance against the manoeuvres to acquire one of the brightest talents from their youth academy.” Losing such a highly rated wonderkid will be a major blow to United’s aspirations, but the 20-time English league champions ended up taking the right call as they should not be held to ransom by a teenager’s father. The move has been made possible as the player possesses an EU passport through his family, which helps him bypass post-Brexit rules that prevent players from moving before the age of 18. A new era under Pochettino There were complaints that Michael Carrick did not place his trust in the club’s famed Carrington academy as much as people would have liked, but United’s new boss Mauricio Pochettino is the polar opposite. item.title: Houston Comets missed No. 1 pick in WNBA draft. Their bigger plans are just beginning
item.description: Heading into the WNBA draft lottery on Sunday, Nov. 15, everything seemed set up for the Houston Comets to jump start the franchise's return by landing the No. 1 pick in the 2027 draft. Houston was tied with the Toronto Tempo for the best odds to receive the top pick and the presumed opportunity to draft USC star JuJu Watkins. The Comets even sent USC legend Tina Thompson, the franchise's No. 1 pick in the WNBA's inaugural 1997 draft, to represent the team onstage at the lottery at ESPN's studios in Bristol, Connecticut. Instead, the No. 1 pick went to Toronto and Houston received the No. 2 pick. But the Comets are focused on what lies ahead, not what could have been. Comets general manager Morgan Tuck said the lottery results won't change the team's outlook for April's draft or for WNBA free agency this winter, which she hopes will deliver a "transformative" offseason for Houston. "Everybody wants to be number one, right? That's just, I think, in our nature," Tuck said on Monday, Nov. 16. "We were very intentional about making sure that we were setting ourselves up for this free agent period and this offseason to be transformative for us. So we get to build off some of the youth that we've currently had, adding a really good young player that can maybe have a little more impact, and then we have a ton of cap flexibility, right? We want to go get some top free agents. We want to have those difference makers that are veterans, and we positioned ourselves to be able to do that." The Comets and every other WNBA team also have to be mindful of another wrinkle: Thanks to the NCAA's new age-based eligibility rule, which allows college athletes five seasons of competition within a five-year window, some of the best players in the WNBA's 2027 draft class – including projected lottery picks Watkins, Texas forward Madison Booker and Notre Dame guard Hannah Hidalgo – could decide to play another year in college instead of entering the draft. That places extra importance on contingency plans, Tuck said. "When you're making a selection in the draft, you just have to plan a little bit further out, right? You can't say, 'Yep, 100%, this is going to be our person,'" Tuck said. "We have some targets that we're obviously going to watch, but we're going to keep it pretty widespread and make sure that we're seeing everybody that we need to so if someone ends up going back or isn't available, we feel good about our decision." The Comets are inheriting several players and staff members from the Connecticut Sun, who were sold last spring and relocated to Houston. The Sun went 22-66 over the last two seasons while in rebuilding mode. Comets guard Saniya Rivers, who averaged 6.9 points and 3.1 assists for Connecticut last season, told USA TODAY Sports that the move to Houston and securing the No. 2 draft pick is a chance at a "fresh start."
